criteria.criterion: The change description names the root cause: the failed-check record stores the last N lines of the log without regard to what they are, so CI post-job cleanup text displaces the test runner's failing section. It is fixed in one shared function in crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs that both the local run and the CI-log path (gh/client.rs detail_from_job_logs and with_failure_detail) call.
criteria.evidence: I read the diff. The doc comment on the new `pub fn failure_section` in checks.rs says: "The old rule kept the last N lines whatever they were, so for a CI log the post-job cleanup text displaced the test runner's `failures:` and `panicked at` section." The CHANGELOG entry repeats this. The three old `tail(&tail_lines(..))` sites are gone. run_check (failed branch), with_failure_detail and detail_from_job_logs now all call failure_section. The snapshot's commit messages are just "base" and "candidate", so the doc comment and the CHANGELOG are the change description I could check.

criteria.criterion: A new unit test in checks.rs, run with `cargo test -p athena-core checks`, feeds a log with a `failures:` section, a `panicked at` line and a `test result: FAILED` line followed by more than 200 lines of post-job cleanup, as in the CI logs of jobs 20261106-022423-vdtn and 20261106-045349-f6x6. It asserts the kept output contains the failing test name and the assertion text and no `Post job cleanup` lines. The test fails on the base commit (verify with git stash or the fails-without run) and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: 76 tests passed, including failure_section_drops_trailing_cleanup_and_keeps_the_failing_section (250 cleanup lines after the failures:/panicked at/test result: FAILED section; checks the test name and assertion text are kept and no `Post job cleanup` remains) and a_failed_local_run_keeps_the_failing_section_not_trailing_cleanup (goes through run_check). Athena's fails-without-2 run on the reverted tree exited 101, but only because failure_section did not exist there, so the tests did not compile. The run_check test calls only functions the base already has. On the base, the last 200 of its 254 output lines are all `Post job cleanup.`, so its assertions would fail. That last point is reasoning from the base code; I could not run it, because git stash is not allowed here.

criteria.criterion: A test in gh/tests.rs, run with `cargo test -p athena-core gh`, builds a CI job log whose failing output has no parseable `test ... FAILED` names (for example a panic in an xtask test) followed by cleanup text. It asserts detail_from_job_logs returns an output_tail with the panic message and not the cleanup lines. It fails on the base and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: 155 tests passed, including cleanup_after_an_xtask_panic_does_not_displace_it (an xtask `repin` panic, no `test ... FAILED` line, 250 stamped cleanup lines; checks failed_tests is empty, `pin mismatch` is in output_tail and no `Post job cleanup` is). two_shards_each_keep_their_failing_section also passed. On the base, detail_from_job_logs kept the last 200 lines of a 253-line log, and every one of those is cleanup, so the assertions would fail. Athena's fails-without-3 run failed only because the checks.rs tests did not compile.

criteria.criterion: A log with no runner marker and no cleanup text keeps the same output as today (tail of the last FAILED_TAIL_LINES lines), and a passing check's kept output is unchanged. Existing tests, including red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail and the run/tests.rs reuse test, still pass under `cargo test --locked`.
criteria.evidence: failure_section_without_marker_or_cleanup_is_the_old_tail checks with assert_eq that the output equals the old `tail(&tail_lines(text,200), FAILED_TAIL_BYTES)`, both with no marker and with a marker inside the window. The passing branch of run_check (`tail(&output, TAIL_BYTES)`) is unchanged in the diff. These existing tests passed in my runs: a_failed_run_keeps_its_last_200_lines_and_a_passing_run_its_byte_tail, red_reused_run_records_failing_tests_and_log_tail, and the ci_reuse_red/green tests in run::tests. Athena's recorded `cargo test --locked` passed (reused from CI run 42392344666 for 2a7cbfc3).

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has one entry under Fixed or Changed stating that a failed check record now keeps the failing test section instead of the log tail. It states only what the diff does.

It says a failed check's record now keeps the failing test section, with CI post-job cleanup dropped, instead of the last 200 lines, and that `checks::failure_section` does this for a local run, a reused CI run's detail and each CI job log. That matches the diff.

findings.summary: In the jump case, failure_section returns max_lines + 1 lines, one more than the cap
findings.evidence: In the jump case the output is `head` (max_lines - SECTION_END_LINES lines), then a `…` line, then SECTION_END_LINES lines: 201 lines when the cap is 200. In detail_from_job_logs with 2 shards, each section can be 100 lines plus a `== name` header, 202 in total. with_failure_detail then cuts that to 199, which can drop the first shard's header and the first lines of its section. Fix: make the head max_lines - SECTION_END_LINES - 1 lines.

findings.summary: The fails-without evidence is a compile error, not a failed assertion
findings.evidence: Athena's fails-without-2/3/4 runs exited 101 with E0425 (`failure_section` not found). The behavioral tests (a_failed_local_run_..., cleanup_after_an_xtask_panic_..., two_shards_...) use only functions the base has, and the base code shows they would fail their assertions. But no run actually showed those assertion failures. Keeping the direct failure_section unit tests and the entry-point tests in separate places would let the revert run show real assertion failures.

findings.summary: With no runner marker and no `##[error]` line, the cleanup cut can fire on the first matching line anywhere in the log
findings.evidence: With no marker and no `##[error]` line, the anchor is line 0 and the cut is the first line starting with `Post job cleanup`, `Post Run ` or `Cleaning up orphan processes` at index > 0. Everything after that line is dropped. Such text is unlikely in local output, but it is a false positive the code does not guard against. Cutting only when the cleanup block runs to the end of the log, or only in the CI path, would be tighter. (Estimate: rare in practice.)

findings.summary: No test covers the most realistic layout of a real log
findings.evidence: The real record in the evidence snapshot (records/jobs/2026-11/20261106-045349-f6x6/verification.json) shows the failing unit's section far back in the log. Over 180 lines of passing units' output follow it, then about 20 cleanup lines. The code handles this: the cut, then the jump case. But no single test feeds section + more than 200 passing lines + cleanup. The jump test and the cleanup tests each cover half of it.

summary: The change passes: all seven criteria are met and no finding is major or blocking. It adds one shared function, `checks::failure_section`. The function drops CI post-job cleanup lines from the end of a log and keeps the test runner's failing section (the `failures:`, `panicked at` and `test result: FAILED` lines). When the last 200 lines contain none of those lines, it starts from the earliest one and adds the final 20 lines. All three places that used to store "the last 200 lines" now use it: the local check run, the step that adds detail to a reused CI result (with_failure_detail), and the CI job-log reader (detail_from_job_logs). I ran `cargo test -p athena-core checks` (76 passed) and `cargo test -p athena-core gh` (155 passed), which include the new tests and the existing reuse and log-tail tests. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test results passed on this commit. I also traced the fix by hand against a real stored record from job 20261106-045349-f6x6. The new rule would keep that job's failing section, which the old rule lost. There are four small findings: (1) in the jump case the stored output can be 201 lines, one over the 200 cap; (2) Athena's fails-without runs failed only because the code did not compile, not on test assertions, though the base code shows the assertions would fail; (3) a log with no test-runner lines could be cut at a stray line that merely looks like cleanup; (4) no single test combines a far-back failing section, passing output and cleanup. The CHANGELOG entry is accurate, and every changed file is on the deliverables list.
